plugins.otoroshi.io.Workflow.description: A workflow of the workflows extension: a json tree of nodes (function calls, control flow, data transformations) that otoroshi runs on demand through the api, as a scheduled job, or from a route through the workflow plugins (backend, request and response transformers)

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams the workflow belongs to. The default tenant and team when absent

id.description: The unique id of the workflow, used to call it, to schedule it and to reference it from a plugin or from another workflow

name.description: The display name of the workflow, shown and searched in the list of the workflows of the backoffice

description.description: A free text describing what the workflow does, shown and searched in the list of the workflows of the backoffice
description.example: Greets the name given as input and logs the greeting

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the workflow, with string values. The admin api stores the date of the last write of the entity under `created_at` or `updated_at`

tags.description: Free tags of the workflow, to sort and search the workflows

config.description: The root node of the workflow, run with the input of the workflow (available to the nodes as `workflow_input`). A node is a json object whose `kind` selects what it does, its other fields depend on its kind: a `workflow` node runs its `steps` (an array of nodes) in sequence, a `call` node calls the function named by `function` with its `args`, `if`, `switch`, `foreach`, `map`, `filter`, `flatmap`, `parallel`, `while`, `try`, `jump` and `async` nodes hold other nodes. The strings of a node can read the memory of the run with `${<name>}` or `${<name>.<path>}`, and objects with a single key starting with `$` are operators (`$mem_ref`, `$str_concat`, `$eq`, ...). An empty object when absent

id.description: The id of the node, shown in the logs, the errors and the debugger of the run. A random id when absent

kind.description: The kind of the node: `workflow`, `call`, `assign`, `value`, `if`, `switch`, `foreach`, `map`, `filter`, `flatmap`, `parallel`, `while`, `try`, `jump`, `async`, `wait`, `error`, `pause`, `end` or `breakpoint`, or the kind of a node registered by an extension. A node of an unknown kind does nothing

description.description: What the node does, for the readers of the workflow
description.example: Greets the input name then logs the greeting

enabled.description: Whether the node runs, true when absent. A disabled node is skipped and returns null

breakpoint.description: Whether the debugger of the editor pauses the run before this node, false when absent

result.description: The name of the memory slot the result of the node is stored in, for the next nodes to read it with `${<name>}`

returned.description: A json value that replaces the output of the node, its operators applied first (for instance `{"$mem_ref": {"name": "call_res"}}` returns the content of the memory slot `call_res`)

example.description: Greets the input name then logs the greeting

test_payload.description: The input sent to the workflow when it is run from the editor of the backoffice, available to the nodes as `workflow_input`. Free json object, `{"name": "foo"}` when absent

orphans.description: The nodes of the editor canvas that are not connected to the tree of the workflow, kept with the edges between them so that the editor shows them again. They are never run

nodes.description: The nodes that are not connected to the tree of the workflow

items.description: A workflow node (the same shape as `config`) with its place on the canvas

id.description: The id of the node, that the `source` and `target` of the edges name

kind.description: The kind of the node, as in `config`

position.description: The position of the node on the canvas, in pixels

edges.description: The edges of the canvas that start from or end at an orphan node

items.description: An edge of the editor canvas between two nodes. Free json object, the editor writes the fields below

id.description: The id of the edge on the canvas, generated by the editor

source.description: The id of the node the edge starts from

target.description: The id of the node the edge ends at

sourceHandle.description: The handle of the source node the edge starts from

targetHandle.description: The handle of the target node the edge ends at

type.description: The kind of edge drawn by the editor

animated.description: Whether the editor animates the edge

job.description: Runs the workflow as a job of otoroshi: once, at a fixed interval or on a cron expression. Not scheduled when absent

functions.description: The functions of the workflow, by name: nodes a `call` node of the workflow runs with `"function": "self.<name>"`, the arguments of the call being available to the function as `function_args`. Empty when absent

additionalProperties.description: The node run when the function is called, the same shape as `config`

id.description: The id of the root node of the function, shown in the logs, the errors and the debugger of the run

kind.description: The kind of the node, as in `config`

notes.description: The notes placed on the canvas of the editor. They are not part of the workflow, and a note without `id`, `kind`, `position` or `measured` makes otoroshi drop every note

items.description: A note of the editor canvas: a text box with its colors, its place and its size

content.description: The text of the note, empty when absent

color.description: The background color of the note, a css color, `var(--bg-color_level3)` when absent

titleColor.description: The color of the text of the note, a css color, `#fff` when absent

position.description: The position of the note on the canvas, in pixels

measured.description: The size of the note on the canvas, in pixels

width.description: The width of the note, in pixels

height.description: The height of the note, in pixels

id.description: The id of the note on the canvas

kind.description: The kind of the canvas node, `note` for a note

example.name: Greet and log
example.description: Greets the name given as input and logs the greeting

config.description: Greets the input name then logs the greeting

WorkflowJobConfig.description: How a workflow runs as a job of otoroshi, and the input of each run. The job is scheduled as soon as the workflow is saved with `enabled` true, and stopped when it is disabled or deleted. A job without `kind` or `instantiation` is read as the default job (disabled)

enabled.description: Whether the workflow is scheduled as a job, false when absent

kind.description: When the job runs: `ScheduledOnce` once after `initial_delay`, `ScheduledEvery` after `initial_delay` then every `interval`, `Cron` on `cron_expression`, `Autonomous` once after `initial_delay`. Read without case, an unknown value is read as `ScheduledEvery`

instantiation.description: Where the job runs in a cluster: `OneInstancePerOtoroshiInstance` on every instance, `OneInstancePerOtoroshiWorkerInstance` on every worker, `OneInstancePerOtoroshiLeaderInstance` on every leader, `OneInstancePerOtoroshiCluster` on a single instance of the cluster. Read without case, an unknown value is read as `OneInstancePerOtoroshiInstance`

initial_delay.description: The delay before the first run, in milliseconds. No delay when null

interval.description: The delay between two runs of a `ScheduledEvery` job, in milliseconds. A `ScheduledEvery` job without interval only runs once

cron_expression.description: The quartz cron expression (seconds, minutes, hours, day of month, month, day of week) of a `Cron` job

config.description: The input of the workflow on each run of the job, available to the nodes as `workflow_input`. Free json object, empty when absent

plugins.otoroshi.io.Script.description: A plugin of the legacy engine written in scala and compiled by otoroshi at runtime. Deprecated: the plugins of the new engine, and the wasm plugins, replace it

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams of the script, checked against the rights of the admins

id.description: The unique id of the script, referenced by the routes and the global configuration that use it

name.description: The name of the script, displayed in the backoffice

desc.description: A free text describing what the script does
desc.example: Adds a header to every request

code.description: The scala code of the script: a class extending the base class of its `type`, compiled when the script is saved

type.description: What the script is: `app`, `transformer` (the default), `validator` (access validator), `preroute`, `sink`, `listener` (event listener), `job`, `exporter` (data exporter), `request-handler`, `tunnel-handler` or `composite`. An unknown type reads as `transformer`

metadata.description: Free metadata of the script, as string keys and values

tags.description: Free tags of the script, used to sort and find it in the backoffice

example.name: New request transformer

plugins.otoroshi.io.WasmPlugin.description: A wasm plugin: a webassembly module and the way to run it, that the wasm plugins of the routes, of the apis and of the global configuration reference by its id instead of repeating its configuration

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams of the wasm plugin, checked against the rights of the admins

id.description: The unique id of the wasm plugin, the reference the wasm plugins of the routes use (`Local` source kind)

name.description: The name of the wasm plugin, displayed in the backoffice

description.description: A free text describing what the wasm plugin does
description.example: Checks the api key of the calls against a remote registry

config.description: The webassembly module and how it runs. A missing config reads as the default one

steps.description: The steps of a route the plugin can be used at, to offer it in the backoffice. A step otoroshi does not know is left out

items.description: A step of the proxy engine

metadata.description: Free metadata of the wasm plugin, as string keys and values

tags.description: Free tags of the wasm plugin, used to sort and find it in the backoffice

WasmVmKillOptions.description: When an instance of a wasm module is killed and replaced by a fresh one, to bound the memory and the state it accumulates

max_calls.description: The number of calls after which the instance is killed. 2147483647 (no limit) when absent

max_memory_usage.description: The ratio of its memory the instance can use before it is killed, between 0 and 1. 0 (no limit) when absent

max_avg_call_duration.description: The average duration of the calls, in milliseconds, above which the instance is killed. 0 (no limit) when absent

max_unused_duration.description: The time without any call, in milliseconds, after which the instance is killed. 300000 (5 minutes) when absent

WasmConfig.description: A webassembly module and the way otoroshi runs it: where its wasm comes from, the function to call, what the module is allowed to reach, and how many instances run it

source.description: Where the wasm of the module comes from. The legacy `compiler_source` (a wasmo plugin) and `raw_source` (an url, `file://`, `base64://`, `entity://` or `local://`) keys are read when it is absent

memoryPages.description: The memory of an instance, in pages of 64 KiB. 100 when absent

functionName.description: The function of the module to call. Each kind of plugin calls its own default function when null

config.description: The configuration handed to the module, as string keys and values

allowedHosts.description: The hosts the module can call with the http request function of its runtime (the `allowed_hosts` of the extism manifest)

allowedPaths.description: The directories of the host the module can reach through wasi (the `allowed_paths` of the extism manifest): the path on the host as key, the path the module sees as value

wasi.description: Run the module with the wasi support: files, environment, http calls through the allowed hosts

opa.description: The module is an open policy agent policy compiled to wasm, evaluated as such

httpWasm.description: The module implements the http-wasm abi (http handlers), called as such

authorizations.description: What the module can reach in otoroshi. The legacy `accesses` key is read when it is absent

instances.description: The number of instances of the module kept to serve the calls in parallel

killOptions.description: When an instance of the module is killed and replaced by a fresh one

isJS.description: The module is javascript compiled to wasm (javy), run with its runtime

WasmSource.description: Where the wasm of a module comes from

kind.description: The kind of source: `Base64` (the module itself, base64 encoded, in `path`), `Http` (an url), `Wasmo` (a plugin built by the wasmo of the global configuration), `Local` (another wasm plugin, by id), `File` (a file of the host), `ClassPath` (a resource of the classpath of otoroshi), `Unknown` when none. Read whatever its case, `wasmmanager` being read as `Wasmo`

path.description: The module, where to find it: the base64 module, the url, the wasmo plugin name, the id of the wasm plugin, the file path or the classpath resource, depending on the kind

opts.description: The options of the source. `Http`: `method`, `headers`, `timeout` (milliseconds), `followRedirect`, `proxy` and `tls`. `Wasmo`: `follow_redirect` and `timeout` (milliseconds)

WasmDataRights.description: A read and a write right

WasmAuthorizations.description: What a wasm module can reach in otoroshi through the functions of the host. Everything is denied by default

httpAccess.description: The module can make http calls through otoroshi

proxyHttpCallTimeout.description: The timeout of these http calls, in milliseconds

globalDataStoreAccess.description: Access to the whole datastore of otoroshi

pluginDataStoreAccess.description: Access to the keys of the datastore of the plugin only

globalMapAccess.description: Access to the in memory map shared by every plugin

pluginMapAccess.description: Access to the in memory map of the plugin only

proxyStateAccess.description: The module can read the state of the proxy: routes, backends, api keys, certificates...

configurationAccess.description: The module can read the configuration of otoroshi
